rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Nepal's vegetation is strongly zoned by altitude and climate. The Terai supports subtropical sal forests and grasslands; the sub-montane and temperate hills have mixed deciduous and broadleaf forests dominated by rhododendron, oak, and chestnut; the sub-alpine zone is coniferous (pine, fir, juniper); the alpine zone has meadows, dwarf shrubs, and lichens; and the nival zone is bare rock and snow.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Vegetation zones (altitude): Terai (60–1000 m) → Sub-montane (500–1500 m) → Temperate (1000–2000 m) → Sub-alpine (2000–3000 m) → Alpine (>3000 m) → Nival (>4500 m)
Dominant species: sal (Terai), rhododendron + oak (temperate), pine + fir (sub-alpine), meadows + lichens (alpine)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Vegetation zones are defined by ALTITUDE + climate (rainfall, temperature), not by political boundaries.  ·  Sal (Shorea robusta) is the dominant Terai/subtropical tree; rhododendron dominates the temperate hills.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: NEB expects the altitude-based vegetation zones with dominant species for each.  ·  Sal (Terai) and rhododendron (temperate) are the key species to know.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Terai: sal forest (Shorea robusta), banyan, peepal; Chitwan grasslands.  ·  Sub-montane: mixed deciduous — rhododendron, oak, laurel, alder.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Burning/shifting agriculture (jhum) degrades vegetation; natural regrowth is slow on poor soils.  ·  Temperate forests (oak, rhododendron, chestnut) differ from subtropical (sal, peepal) in species and altitude.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Zones: Terai → Sub-montane → Temperate → Sub-alpine → Alpine → Nival (rising).  ·  Sal = Terai; Rhododendron + Oak = temperate; Pine + Fir = sub-alpine; Meadows = alpine.

rows.text: List Nepal's vegetation zones by altitude with dominant species.  ·  Explain the vegetation of the Terai (sal forest, grasslands).

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Explain the Terai vegetation (sal forest, grasslands).  ·  Describe the temperate vegetation (rhododendron, oak, chestnut).

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Altitude-based vegetation zones  ·  Terai sal forest  ·  Temperate rhododendron-oak forest  ·  Sub-alpine coniferous forest

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Vegetation is set by altitude + climate (temperature, rainfall) + soil + human activity.  ·  Nepal zones: Terai → Sub-montane → Temperate → Sub-alpine → Alpine → Nival.  ·  Terai: sal forest + grasslands (warm, low rainfall).  ·  Temperate: oak, rhododendron (national flower), chestnut.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: About 64% of Nepal's area is under forest; ~35% is evergreen.  ·  Rhododendron arboreum, the national flower, dominates the temperate hills (1000–3000 m).

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: Describe the temperate vegetation of the hills.  ·  Explain the sub-alpine and alpine vegetation.  ·  Discuss the impact of human activities on Nepali vegetation.

rows.label: More hints
rows.text: What is the tree line and where does it end in the Himalaya?

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: Temperate: oak (Quercus), rhododendron (Rhododendron arboreum), chestnut.  ·  Sub-alpine: pine (Pinus wallichiana), fir (Abies), juniper.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: Vegetation: the natural plant cover of a region, determined by climate (temperature, rainfall), altitude, soil, and human activities.  ·  Nepal vegetation zones (by altitude):  ·  Terai/subtropical (60–1000 m): sal (Shorea robusta), banyan, peepal, grasslands (Chitwan, Bardia); warm, low humidity.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Human impact (jhum, grazing)  ·  Dominant species  ·  Sub-alpine: pine, fir, juniper; Alpine: meadows, dwarf shrubs, lichens.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Human impact: deforestation (firewood, jhum, grazing, over-exploitation).  ·  Chitwan sal forest supports tiger and rhino; ~64% of Nepal is forested.  ·  Alpine zone has meadows and dwarf shrubs, NOT tall trees; the "tree line" ends around 3000–4000 m.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Vegetation is the NATURAL plant cover; "plantations" and "cultivated crops" are human-made, not natural vegetation.  ·  Alpine: meadows, dwarf shrubs, lichens, mosses (e.g., Everest region).  ·  Nival: bare rock, snow, sparse lichens and mosses (>4500 m).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: The tree line ends at ~3000–4500 m; above it only dwarf shrubs and meadows grow.  ·  Human impact: deforestation, jhum (shifting agriculture), grazing, over-exploitation.  ·  Give specific Nepali examples (Chitwan sal, Everest alpine meadows).
